meta.title: How it works
meta.description: The plan in four steps: print PLA parts, seal half with epoxy, run 20 cycles of 70% isopropyl alcohol disinfection, and measure what changed.

lead: This is the plan, in the order it will happen. Nothing has been measured yet.
figureNote: Illustration, not a photo of my setup.

steps.name: Print
text: Every part is printed in PLA from one spool, on one printer, with the same settings.
The test bars are about 80 × 10 × 4 mm. After printing, each part is weighed and randomly put into one of four groups.
steps.note: 8 extra pilot bars are printed first for practice. They are not part of the data.
steps.alt: Drawing of a printer nozzle laying down a line of plastic on top of four finished layers of a test bar about 80 mm long.

steps.name: Seal
text: Half of the parts get two thin brushed coats of Smooth-On XTC-3D, an epoxy made for coating 3D prints.
The second coat goes on once the first is no longer tacky. Then the parts cure for 24 hours before any alcohol touches them.
steps.alt: Drawing of a brush putting a green coat of epoxy around a printed test bar.

steps.name: Disinfect
text: Half of the sealed parts and half of the unsealed parts go through 20 disinfection cycles.
One cycle is 60 seconds fully under 70% isopropyl alcohol in a closed jar, then 20 minutes on a drying rack.
The other parts get 0 cycles, but they are handled and stored the same way.
steps.note: At 3 cycles a day, that is about 7 lab days.
steps.alt: Drawing of a test bar inside a closed jar of liquid for 60 seconds, then on a drying rack for 20 minutes, with arrows showing the loop repeats 20 times.

steps.name: Measure
steps.kicker: Four measurements, done the same way every time
text: Every part is weighed three times: as printed, after the epoxy cures, and after the cycles. Each bend bar is also measured at the same three marked points each time.
Then 20 bars are bent until they break, and 20 bars are soaked in dyed water to see how much liquid gets in.
steps.alt: Drawing of a three-point bend test: a test bar resting on two supports 64 mm apart, with a force pushing down on the middle.

gaps.label: The idea being tested
gaps.heading: Same part, with and without a seal.
gaps.caption: A printed part isn't solid. The gaps between layers can let liquid in.
gaps.disclaimer: Illustration of the idea, not results.

unsealed.title: Unsealed
unsealed.text: Liquid can get into the gaps between the printed lines and stay inside the part.
unsealed.alt: Drawing of a slice through an unsealed printed part. Liquid runs down through the gaps between the plastic lines and collects inside.

sealed.title: Sealed
sealed.text: The idea is that a coat of epoxy closes the gaps, so liquid stays on the outside. Whether that holds up is what the experiment tests.
sealed.alt: Drawing of a slice through a sealed printed part. A green epoxy layer covers the surface and droplets sit on top of it.

measure.label: What gets measured
measure.heading: Four numbers and one set of photos.

items.name: Liquid absorption
items.how: A dried bar is weighed, soaked in dyed water for 24 hours, blotted the same way every time, and weighed again. The extra weight is the liquid it took in.
items.why: It shows whether the surface is closed.

items.name: Bending strength
items.how: A bar rests on two supports 64 mm apart. A force pushes down on the middle until the bar breaks.
items.why: It shows whether the part stays strong.

items.name: Mass change
items.how: Each part is weighed after the epoxy cures and again after the cycles, on a balance that reads to 0.001 g.
items.why: It shows whether material or coating was lost.

items.name: Size change
items.how: Thickness is measured at three marked points on each bend bar, before and after the cycles.

items.name: Dye photos
items.how: At least one soaked bar from each group is snapped open and photographed, to show how far the dyed water got inside.
items.why: It makes the path of the liquid visible. It is a picture, not a number.

measure.note: Soaking up a test liquid stands in for holding on to disinfectant. It is not a direct measurement of it.
